item.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
item.description: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.
item.dc:creator: The Hacker News

item.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
item.description: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated. Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). item.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
item.description: Right now, there is probably an AI agent running on a laptop somewhere in your network. It stores API keys and database passwords, can access your internal systems, and works without anyone watching. Nobody reviewed its access. Nobody owns it. If an employee had that much reach with that little oversight, you would call it an insider risk. So why do we still call the agent a productivity tool?
